text:
alex: Quick sync: finalizing the GA default for private-deploy networking. We have three delivery patterns: shared relay (fast onramp), customer-managed egress (static IPs / token proof), and peering (BGP/dedicated). I want a proposal that covers default + upgrade paths + a migration "plan" object that operators and CS can use.

priya: My strong preference is shared relay as the GA default, but with 2 additions: 1) per-tenant "egress profile" metadata (static|burstable|dedicated) so we can size pools, 2) a canary mode that lets us route a small % of traffic via customer-egress during validation.

morgan: Relay default is pragmatic. Unique ask: support "egress plans" in the API so migrations are declarative and reversible. Example builder: POST /v1/tenants/:id/egress-plans -> { "plan_id":"fast-onramp-v1", "steps":[{"type":"validate"},{"type":"cutover","drain_secs":30,"warm_secs":60}], "rollback": {"on_failure": "revert_to_relay"} }

netops-cam: Important ops constraints: segmented relay pools per-region to prevent cross-tenant noisy-neighbor issues, IP rotation windows (7d min), and hard quotas for ephemeral pools. If we do canaries, we need traffic-sampling hooks and per-tenant telemetry.

cs-lin: Field preference: self-serve for customer-egress but include an ownership proof flow that doesn't require their infra team to open ports to our agent. Suggest: we serve a short-lived signed token + URL; customer curls that URL from their egress IP and we validate the source IP matches. That avoids reverse-DNS flakiness.

alex: Nice. Let's also capture IPv6: acceptance should include either NAT64 support in relay or explicit docs that IPv6-only egress requires customer-egress with IPv4 translation.

priya: Fallback semantics proposal: agent validates target egress every 30s; on 3 consecutive failures mark degraded and swing traffic back to relay. Provide an "operator lock" to opt out of auto-fallback for customers that accept risk. All transitions write audit events.

morgan: API sketch for declarative toggle + dry-run:
```
POST /v1/tenants/:tid/connectivity
{ "mode":"relay|egress|peering", "plan_id":"fast-onramp-v1", "egress_ips":["203.0.113.42"], "canary_pct":5 }

POST /v1/tenants/:tid/connectivity/validate
{ "mode":"egress","egress_ips":["203.0.113.42"] }
# returns: {"ok":"true","challenges":["token: abc..","probe_ip: 203.0.113.42"]}
```
Dry-run should surface expected failure modes and a cost-estimate delta for relay vs egress.

netops-cam: For peering: gate behind Dedicated/contract and require checklist items (ASN, prefix filters, test mirror). Do not route peering as a default.

cs-lin: Acceptance criteria for GA (suggested):
- Default path: shared relay + regional pools documented, onboarding template works w/ minimal firewall changes
- Egress profiles: per-tenant metadata and canary mechanism implemented
- Declarative migration: egress-plan object + validate endpoint + dry-run in API
- Fallback & audit: automatic revert after 3 failed probes + operator lock + audit trail visible in Console
- Ownership proof flow: signed-token curl verification for customer-egress
- IPv6 story: relay supports NAT64 OR docs + validation for IPv6-only customers
- Peering: documented + gated for Dedicated only

ops-bot: ops-bot: Draft doc created: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/egress-plans-and-canaries (comments open) :robot_face:

alex: Action items: Priya -> implement egress-profile metadata + canary plumbing; Morgan -> design plan object and dry-run response; Cam -> relay pool segmentation and IP-rotation policy; Lin -> CS ownership-proof template and console status UI; I'll update roadmap ticket with the GA acceptance criteria above and add a migration playbook stub.

(ended)
